newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Liberia peacekeepers prepare fresh deployment.
newsitem.headline: Liberia peacekeepers prepare fresh deployment.

text.p: West African peacekeepers in Liberia have sent an advance contingent to the southeastern port of Greenville to prepare the ground for a major deployment in the town, a spokesman said on Thursday.

The deployment, in an area where supporters of faction leader Charles Taylor are fighting ethnic Krahn rivals, will be the first new deployment outside the capital Monrovia since the six-year-old civil war flared there in April and May.
"We have deployed our tactical unit in Greenville. They are there to ensure the battalion that we are sending there later this week is deployed safely," the spokesman told Reuters.
A battalion of over 1,000 men from the Nigerian-led force is due to deploy in and around the port, where militia groups are suspected of exporting timber illegally.

Force commander Victor Malu, promised reinforcements to double its strength to 18,000, had previously said he would not deploy further outside Monrovia until extra men arrived. The force patrols main roads to hot spots in the west and is in Kakata north of Monrovia, Buchanan port and Harbel in the east.
Freed American slaves set up Liberia in 1847. The war, launched by Taylor in late 1989, is rooted in rivalry between descendents of the slaves and the original inhabitants.
The war has killed well over 150,000 people, hundreds of them in fighting and looting in Monrovia in April and May.

West African leaders rallied the faction leaders around a peace plan in Nigeria in August. It envisaged disarmament by January and elections by May, with the threat of individual sanctions against anyone derailing the deal.
